crop.notes: The whole item, headline 'A Fight Between McCoole and Allen in Prospect' through 'this evening'.

ocr.notes: Gist readable but many garbled words and names ('MoCeoLe', 'Eagl#sh', 'Whes-nut' for Chesnut, 'Alb ,.' for Allen).

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that after a $1,000 wager in a Chesnut Street saloon, Mike McCoole agreed to fight Tom Allen for any sum from $1,000 to $10,000. Allen claimed to be the champion of England in America.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'The Missouri Republican--St. Louis, March 8, 1869'. The saloon meeting was 'Saturday evening', March 6, 1869.

facts.fact: After his fight with Charley Gallagher, Allen kept demanding another fight, saying he was able and willing to fight any man in America
At a Chesnut Street saloon Allen asserted McCoole could not whip him in an hour and a half; a $1,000 wager was made and a $50 forfeit put up by McCoole's friend was covered by Allen
McCoole consented to fight Allen and said he was ready to fight for any amount from $1,000 to $10,000
Allen claimed to be the champion of England in America

notes: The existing fact 'Allen claims English championship title when he came to America the first time' has no unique id in the index (000), so it is not linked.
